messages:
Maya Patel: hi all, day 1 here! trying to attach a service account to a GCE instance and assume an AWS role for a cross-cloud test but getting permission errors on both. not sure who to flag for billing/role attachments.

Diego Ramos: welcome Maya :tada: what errors are you seeing?

Maya Patel: for GCP: `ERROR: (gcloud.compute.instances.create) Permission 'serviceaccounts.serviceAccounts.actAs' denied.` For AWS: `is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole`. also when I look at Billing -> linked projects I don't see my project.

Sasha (infra-oncall): pinging infra. quick checklist: did you create the project using the onboarding template? which project id?

Maya Patel: project is `redwood-maya-test`. created from the quickstart button.

Billing Bot: automated note: projects created via quickstart are not auto-linked to billing if a cost-center tag is missing. Please add label `cost_center=eng` or request billing attach via https://go.redwood/billing-attach.

Maya Patel: ah that explains it. where do I add the label?

Diego Ramos: `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding ...` is for IAM; for labels do `gcloud projects update redwood-maya-test --update-labels=cost_center=eng,owner=maya`. finance will pick it up.

Sasha (infra-oncall): I checked IAM: your project only has `roles/viewer` for the group `redwood-devs`. That explains the SA actAs error. I'll add `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` to the sandbox service account for you and attach `roles/editor` to the project temporarily.

Onboarding Bot: Reminder: new hires must confirm they completed the cloud security checklist: https://go.redwood/cloud-checklist. Skipping will block some permissions.

Maya Patel: thanks Sasha. any ETA? I need to run a 50-rqps smoke on us-central1 and try the cross-cloud flow.

Sasha (infra-oncall): done. added `serviceAccount:redwood-sandbox-sa@redwood-dev.iam.gserviceaccount.com` as member with `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` and temporarily attached `roles/editor` to your project. also linked billing `redwood-dev-billing` to `redwood-maya-test`. should be immediate but give it a minute.

Maya Patel: I retried the gcloud command and it worked! `gcloud compute instances create maya-test-1 --zone=us-central1-a --service-account=redwood-sandbox-sa@redwood-dev.iam.gserviceaccount.com`

Diego Ramos: for the AWS assume role, you'll need to be in the `okta-aws-devs` group or have the IAM role added to your Okta mapping. I added you to the group; logout/login to Okta and run `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/Redwood-Dev-Assume --role-session-name maya-test`.

Maya Patel: ran assume-role, looks good. minor follow-up: how do we request permanent permissions vs temporary sandbox?

Sasha (infra-oncall): file a Permissions Request form (link posted in #new-hires pinned). include justification, required roles, and duration. infra reviews weekly on Tues. For region exceptions (if you need asia regions) use the region-request form with traffic estimate.

Maya Patel: perfect. one more Q about cost: any recommended flags to keep the smoke cheap?

Diego Ramos: use `--machine-type=e2-small --preemptible --boot-disk-size=10GB` and add labels `--labels=owner=maya,team=platform`. also terminate after test: `gcloud compute instances delete --quiet maya-test-1`.

Maya Patel: awesome, thanks everyone. tagging this thread as resolved for now. :raised_hands:
